title: Infosys Opens 1.1 Million Square Foot Block at Hyderabad Pocharam Campus
excerpt: Infosys has inaugurated a 1.1 million sq. ft. software development block at its 450-acre Pocharam campus in Hyderabad, adding 10,000 seats to support over 13,000 employees under hybrid working.
body:
• Infosys has inaugurated a new 1.1 million sq. ft. software development block at its Pocharam Development Center in Hyderabad, Telangana, the company announced.
  • The new block adds 10,000 seats and will let Infosys aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model.
  • The 450-acre Pocharam campus already houses seven software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq. ft. of built-up area, serving clients in banking and financial services, retail, life sciences and manufacturing.
  • For jobseekers and clients: this is added delivery capacity, not a stated hiring timetable — Infosys's announcement does not give a separate recruitment schedule for the new block, so the 13,000 figure is supported workforce under hybrid working, not 13,000 announced new jobs.

Infosys has expanded its Pocharam Development Center in Hyderabad, Telangana, with the inauguration of a new software development block covering 1.1 million sq. ft., the company said in its official announcement. The Hindu BusinessLine reported the block was inaugurated on Friday, October 30, 2026, by Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and IT and Industries Minister D Sridhar Babu, in the presence of Infosys Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka.

What the new block adds

Spread across 450 acres, the Pocharam campus currently houses seven software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq. ft. of built-up area, Infosys said. The new block will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model. The distinction between seats and supported workforce reflects hybrid working: not every employee is on campus on the same day.

The inauguration was attended by Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, who is also Minister for Finance, Planning, and Energy, and Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Minister for Information Technology, Electronics & Communications, Industries & Commerce, and Legislative Affairs, along with Infosys leaders including CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka, Executive Vice President Sunil Kumar Dhareshwar and Senior Vice President Niladri Prasad Mishra, according to the company.

What work the campus does

The Pocharam Development Center supports global clients across banking, financial services and insurance, retail, life sciences, and manufacturing, Infosys said. The expansion will further strengthen its capabilities in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services.

"Hyderabad has played a pivotal role in our growth journey, and the expansion of our Pocharam campus reflects our continued commitment to the region."

— Jayesh Sanghrajka, Chief Financial Officer, Infosys

Sanghrajka added, in the company's statement, that the facility "enhances our capacity to scale operations, build specialized talent, and deliver complex transformation programs for global clients," and that as enterprises accelerate adoption of AI, the campus will serve as a strategic hub for that work.

Vikramarka said, according to Infosys, that "Telangana has established itself as a global technology destination" and that the expansion marks "another important milestone, creating opportunities for our youth to participate in the next wave of technology-led growth."

How the building is designed

Aligned with its sustainability commitments, Infosys said the new facility incorporates energy-efficient radiant cooling, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting, wastewater reuse and natural daylight-filled spaces. It also features flexible workspaces, collaborative areas and employee wellness facilities to support a modern, hybrid work environment.

What to watch

Infosys describes itself in the announcement as an AI-first business consulting and technology services company with over 325,000 people working in 59 countries. For diaspora technology professionals and for clients in the United States and elsewhere, the Pocharam expansion is a capacity signal: more Hyderabad delivery space aimed at AI, cloud and cybersecurity programmes. What the announcement does not do is set out a hiring timetable or a client-by-client allocation for the new block, and readers should not read the 13,000 supported-workforce figure as a recruitment announcement.
